audit.whatIsWrong: All seven chart rows render two opposite answers: full phases[0..6].side all read "Irelia" at 7-8/10, content win[0..6] all read "Aurora". The content prose goes further and calls the lane a rout in Aurora's favour — "She's forced into passive farming almost every wave", "no answer to your wave-clear speed", "she can't force a fair trade".
audit.why: The full layer is the coherent half: diff HARD, 8/10 difficulty, 8.5/10 carry threat. Irelia is not passive into Aurora at any stage — Bladesurge dashes 600 to a target and refreshes outright on a Marked target or a kill, so a low-health caster in the wave is a free approach that also heals her, and from 3 Flawless Duet stuns and Marks at 850 to start the reset chain.
audit.corrected: All seven content win[N] flipped to Irelia to match phases[N].side, with all seven phases[N].why and all seven whys[N] rewritten in the same proposal to argue the side they sit under.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Mark-and-reset chain — the only mechanic that matters here — is never stated. Meanwhile Vanguard's Edge is described as a stun in three places: whys[4] ("Between Worlds directly nullifies her ultimate's engage"), spikes[1].text ("sidestep the stun and punish her ult") and mid ("her Vanguard's Edge engage dies to your Between Worlds dodge"). And spikes[3].text credits Aurora's R with "untargetability".
audit.why: Riot's Q text: "If the target is Marked or dies to Bladesurge, its cooldown refreshes." Riot's E text: enemies caught between the converging blades are damaged, stunned AND Marked. So the stun is Flawless Duet, the Mark is what refunds the dash, and the two together are the all-in. Riot's R text has no stun at all — it Marks, then forms a wall that damages and slows enemies walking through it. Aurora's R is a leap with a slowing zone and a cross-zone teleport; no untargetability anywhere in it.
audit.corrected: Stun/Mark/reset chain now carried through winCon, enemyWin, cooldowns, dos/donts, early, mid and the whole chart; Vanguard's Edge re-described as a Mark plus a wall; the untargetability claim removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Defiant Dance is never mentioned, and neither is what it does or does not stop.
audit.why: Riot's W text: she charges a strike that deals more damage the longer she charges, and "She takes reduced physical damage during the charge." PHYSICAL only — which means Aurora's magic damage passes through it untouched. That is a genuinely useful, non-obvious thing for the reader to know, and it also tells them the charge is aimed at a jungler, not at their Q.

audit.whatIsWrong: Bladesurge heals her on every cast and the page never says so; report[8].t's only nod to it is "Add anti-heal early into his sustain" — wrong pronoun and no item named.
audit.why: The brief flags needs-antiheal for this matchup: her sustain through chip damage decides extended trades, and it is attached to the ability she casts most.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds named in report[8], breakdown.feeding and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Irelia is called he/his across the full layer: tldr ("He fights through your patterns"), tradeGood ("he answered"), tradeBad ("his engage"), ahead ("hop his answers"), loading ("his engage"), dontsFull[0].t ("his reach"), dontsFull[0].d ("they run out of answers"), report[8].t ("his sustain"), report[9].t ("Make him flinch"), report[11].t ("his reach").
audit.why: champ-gender lists irelia as female; the owner is "you", so every third-person pronoun here is Irelia.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit, and dosFull[2].d invented a "fifteen-second invitation".
audit.why: Flawless Duet is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10 — 16 seconds at rank 1, not fifteen. Bladesurge is 10s at rank 1 but effectively shorter because it refunds; Vanguard's Edge is 125s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into cooldowns, winCon, loading, ahead, dosFull[2], report[5] and report[9].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.late, phases[6].why and report[10].t built advice on R-the-clump and on "E knockback-slow".

notes: BOTH PACKET SUSPECTNAMES ARE FALSE POSITIVES: "The Weirding's" (spikes[0]) and "Your Spirit Abjuration" (spikes[3]) are Aurora's own correct E and passive names. The detector was matching them against Aurora's ability list and flagging the possessive. Both strings were rewritten anyway for content reasons. CHART: all seven rows contradicted themselves — full sides all "Irelia" at 7-8/10, content win[] all "Aurora". I resolved toward the full layer because it agrees with the page's own diff (HARD, 8/10 difficulty, 8.5/10 carry threat) and because the kit supports it at every stage. The one thing that argues the other way is the win rate: 49.7% over 1342 games is nearly even, which is not what a seven-row sweep usually looks like. If the user wants a split rather than a sweep, level 6 is the row to flip — Between Worlds against a 125-second Vanguard's Edge is the closest Aurora comes to owning a stage, and the full layer already rates that row 7/10 rather than 8/10. FLAG THAT CONTRADICTS RIOT'S TEXT, NOT USED: Flawless Duet carries a derived grounding flag, but Riot's E text says only damaged, stunned and Marked. If it does ground, that is a much bigger deal here than the stun itself, since it would switch off both of Aurora's leaps — worth a real source. UNVERIFIED AND NOT WRITTEN: whether tenacity, Cleanse or QSS shortens the Flawless Duet stun; whether the Mark can be removed or expires on a timer; whether Bladesurge can target Aurora while she is invisible inside W; and whether Aurora's leaps can cross the Vanguard's Edge wall or are blocked by it as terrain.
